label: digit 2 input during the original phase
explanation: Token feature: fires whenever the input token is the digit 2 while the original sequence is being read (t < L), at every position and for every L, with no false positives on dev (precision 1.0, recall 0.995). It does not fire on any other token, on <DEL>, or when 2 is fed back during the copy phase; the only activity outside the predicate is a weak (~0.15 of max) firing in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1 just after a sequence-initial 2 has been echoed, plus a few weak firings on other tokens. In the examples, activation is about 0.75 of max at t=0 and roughly 0.68-0.81 elsewhere; the largest activations (~0.95-1.0) are on a 2 at the end of the sequence (just before <DEL>), often right after c, but this was only seen in examples and not measured systematically.

issues: Core predicate holds up. On test it has precision 1.0, recall 0.995 and F1 0.997, with 0 false positives. The 593 missed steps hold 0.1% of activation mass and all have weak activations (about 0.14-0.17 of max).

The only structured part of the misses is a 2 fed back at recall_idx 1, right after an echoed sequence-initial 2 (402 steps on dev). Its rate is tiny: (phase==2)&(in_tok==2) has precision 0.005. So 'does not fire on fed-back 2s' is essentially true, and the explanation already discloses this residue.

The magnitude claim is overstated if read as a systematic effect. A 2 at the last original position (to_go==0) has a mass share of 0.158 against a step share of 0.153, so its mean activation is only about 3% above average. The 0.95-1.0 values are a tail seen in the examples, not a typical peak. The explanation does hedge this as example-only. The 'after a c' detail was not tested and is unverified.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
